chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:
I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when perfume was uncovered in front of him so that he might look at it, and he was in Ihraam, so he covered his nose with his garment from its aroma.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihraam (ritual consecration)

ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the distinction between the prohibition of applying perfume and merely smelling it during Ihraam, as demonstrated by Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) covering his nose to avoid the scent of the exposed perfume. It underscores the scholarly view that the sensory experience of fragrance, rather than its physical application, is the primary concern in this state of consecration. This practical example serves as a key reference for jurists determining the boundaries of permissible actions while in the sacred state.
